scope: Bounded streaming of generated PDF mesh patch triangles through real viewer RAM/swap/Metal
problem: Real VectorApple.ai failed a 64 MiB viewer qualification budget: generating every visible patch into one array requested 122890176 bytes while 2924186 bytes were already reserved.
implementation: Generate patch triangle arrays lazily in original patch and triangle order. Admit space for at most two 722-triangle arrays during iterator handoff, with color spill and row scratch bounds. Accumulate the same sample map across all patches and normalize once. Shared table and texture admission are retained.
viewer_scope: Selected PDF pages and AI sources; exact RAM lease, swap values and Metal frame preservation, authored tensor edge variants, profiled images and independently referenced soft masks.
oracle_correction: Integer-edge alpha rectangle qualification uses its existing independent analytic unit-pixel area oracle. The Poppler reference has alpha 32 outside rectangle x=8 while the analytic oracle and pre-change decoder have alpha 0. Retain Poppler artifacts; qualify rectangle geometry in the separate exact-area test and color-mask band cases against their existing references.

prior_broad_app_run.scope: Before streaming; latest post-streaming viewer verification is the six PDF tests.

limitations: AI fidelity remains incomplete; unchanged native pixels do not establish correctness against all source variants.
Warm CPU timing is current-state evidence under uncontrolled machine load, not GPU presentation latency or a causal speed comparison.
Parser, patch visibility inventory, function/color-space temporaries and other renderer allocations still prevent a complete RSS-cap claim.
